sections.html:
Ephrata is the county seat and Moses Lake is the largest city. Irrigated farming is the backbone of the local economy. Population reached 99,123 in 2020, spread over 38,635 housing units. Owners occupied 62.2% of occupied homes, and 11.8% of all units were vacant. Levies differ by school district, which means two similar houses can get different bills. Check the parcel record before pricing.

Before you list, pull your own parcel record from the Assessor and compare it with the house as it stands today. Wrong square footage or an outbuilding that was torn down can inflate the value, and fixing it is easier before a buyer asks.

Two offices run this. The Assessor values property; the Treasurer sends bills. The Assessor's roll covers about 61,570 parcels, with ownership and legal descriptions kept current. It does not decide how much tax you pay; voters, state limits and each district's assessed value do.

  • Assessor: Courthouse Annex, Room 107, 35 C Street NW, Ephrata. Phone 509-754-2013. Open weekdays, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
  • Treasurer: 35 C Street NW, Room 204, Ephrata, mailing address P.O. Box 37. Phone 509-754-2010. Open weekdays but closed from noon to 1 p.m.
  • Board of Equalization: handles valuation appeals. For help locating comparable sales, ring the Assessor's Office at 509-754-2011 ext. 2683.

The Treasurer's website has a searchable tax statement for 2025 and 2026 and a parcel lookup, so you can get a payoff picture without a trip to Ephrata. Mailing address changes and quit claim forms also go through that office.

sections.h2: How the Assessor values your house
sections.html:
Valuation happens as of January 1, and all properties get new values every year. An old appeal does not roll forward, so protecting your rights means filing a new petition each year.

Owners of older homes and farmland should note two programs. State law sets April 1 as the deadline for senior and disabled tax deferral applications. Exemption claims for seniors and disabled owners can go in at any time of year and apply to the next year's taxes. Open space (current use) filings count as approved on May 1 unless the Assessor tells you otherwise, and you can apply for the next year's valuation anytime from January 1 through December 31.

Senior exemption income limits were updated for the 2027 tax year. Phone the Assessor for today's limit before you count on any figure.

The bill is split in half, due April 30 and October 31, and a post office postmark counts as paid on time. Late payments pick up interest, and some property types pick up penalties too.

DateWhat happens
January 1Valuation date for real property
April 1Senior and disabled deferral applications due
April 30First half of taxes due
June 13% penalty on delinquent tax, where state law applies it
July 1Last day to petition the Board of Equalization, or 30 days after the notice if later
October 31Second half due (a Saturday in 2026)
December 1Additional 8% penalty on delinquent tax, where state law applies it

Houses and other residential property of four units or fewer pay interest alone, at 9% a year for taxes levied in 2023 and later. Everything else pays 12% a year and both penalties. The rules sit in RCW 84.56.020, and the Assessor posts the calendar on its important dates page.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Grant County assessment?
sections.html:
Talk to the Assessor before anything else. A conversation may fix a record error, and if not, you take the dispute to the Board of Equalization. The petition counts as timely when it lands by July 1 of the assessment year, or within 30 calendar days of the notice date if that gives you more time. Mailed petitions need a postmark inside the window. Nothing is charged to file, and one parcel means one petition.

  • Fill in the parcel number, your contact details, what the property is, the Assessor's number, what you think it is worth and why. Sign, date and attach the notice.
  • Attach comparable sales, repair bids, an appraisal or photos. Sales near January 1 carry the most weight.
  • Supporting evidence added later must be at the Board 21 business days before the hearing.

Expect the Board to start from the assumption that the Assessor got it right. Overcoming that takes clear, cogent and convincing evidence, and your hardship or the size of the bill will not be weighed. You will get at least 30 business days' warning of the hearing date. A written decision usually follows in about two weeks, with 45 days as the statutory outer limit. The losing side may go on to the state Board of Tax Appeals, filing within 30 days.

sections.h2: Paying, and what to do if you are behind
sections.html:
Options are mail, the counter, or Point & Pay online. Online fees are 2.7% for credit cards, 0.95% for debit and $1.30 for an eCheck, and a returned payment carries a $30 fee. Online payments take three to five business days to appear.

The Treasurer posts a delinquent tax payment plan application, plus an interest waiver application for a principal residence heading into foreclosure. The office also holds an annual tax foreclosure sale on the Public Surplus website; the 2026 sale ran November 9 and 10. Owners far behind should phone the Treasurer at 509-754-2010 long before the next sale. Washington law also gives an owner with limited income who lives in the house a chance to ask for interest and penalties to be waived as the third anniversary of delinquency approaches.

sections.h2: Closing on a Grant County sale
sections.html:
At closing, the deed and an excise tax affidavit both go to the Treasurer of the county where the home is. State forms and the exemption code list are linked from the Treasurer's page, plus a lack of probate affidavit for deeds where nobody opened probate.

Sellers normally owe the excise tax on the date of sale. Price sets the state rate and the city adds a local one, so ask the Treasurer for the total for your location. Blank deed and quit claim forms are posted there as well, and if yours needs drafting, a title company or attorney can do it.

A workable order: pull a tax statement and payoff figure, confirm the excise rate, gather the deed and affidavit, and have the title company clear any balance out of proceeds. If the buyer pays cash, no lender signs off, one less thing that can delay closing. Ask the title company early whether it needs a recent statement, since the Treasurer's online tools cover 2025 and 2026.

faqs.q: When are Grant County property taxes due?
faqs.a: One half is owed by April 30 and the rest by October 31. A postmark from the post office works, and late balances pick up interest.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my Grant County assessment?
faqs.a: You have until July 1 of the assessment year, or until 30 calendar days after the value change notice if that date is later. Mailed petitions need a postmark by then, and filing is free.

faqs.q: Does Grant County revalue homes every year?
faqs.a: Yes, every year, and last year's appeal does not carry forward. File a new petition annually.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to pay Grant County taxes online?
faqs.a: Expect 2.7% on credit cards, 0.95% on debit and $1.30 on an eCheck. A check by mail or at the counter has no vendor fee.

faqs.q: Does Grant County hold a tax foreclosure sale?
faqs.a: Yes, annually, on the Public Surplus website. The 2026 edition ran November 9 and 10. Phone 509-754-2010 to learn the next date.
